title: New Pill Offers Hope for Patients with Advanced Pancreatic Cancer
subtitle: A breakthrough drug shows promising results in early trials, potentially changing how doctors treat one of the world's deadliest diseases.

summary.en: A new pill called daraxonrasib is being described as a major medical breakthrough for pancreatic cancer. In a recent clinical trial, the drug helped shrink or stop the growth of tumours in most patients. While doctors warn that it is not yet a guaranteed cure, the results are significantly better than traditional chemotherapy. Experts hope this treatment will lead to longer lives for patients facing this difficult diagnosis. Further large-scale studies are now required to confirm these early, positive findings.
summary.zh: 一種名為 daraxonrasib 的新型藥丸被譽為胰臟癌治療的重大醫學突破。在近期的臨床試驗中，該藥物協助多數患者縮小或抑制了腫瘤生長。雖然醫師提醒這尚未被保證為治癒手段，但結果已顯著優於傳統化學治療。專家期盼此療法能為面臨此艱難診斷的患者延長壽命。目前仍需進一步的大規模研究來證實這些早期的正面發現。

paragraphs.en: A new oral medication called daraxonrasib is being hailed by medical experts as the most significant breakthrough in the treatment of pancreatic cancer in decades. This daily pill, which patients take alongside standard chemotherapy, has shown remarkable ability to shrink or even eliminate tumours in patients with advanced forms of the disease. According to The Guardian Health, the drug works by targeting specific genetic mutations—small changes in the body's DNA—that cause cancer cells to grow uncontrollably.
paragraphs.zh: 一種名為 daraxonrasib 的新型口服藥物，正被醫學專家譽為數十年來胰臟癌治療領域最重要的突破。這種每日服用的藥丸，讓病患在接受標準化學治療的同時搭配使用，已展現出顯著縮小甚至消除晚期癌症患者腫瘤的能力。根據《衛報健康》（The Guardian Health）報導，該藥物的作用機制是針對特定的基因突變，也就是人體去氧核糖核酸（DNA）中導致癌細胞失控生長的微小變化進行標靶治療。

paragraphs.en: Pancreatic cancer is widely considered one of the most difficult diseases to treat. Statistics from The Guardian Health show that it has the lowest survival rate of all common cancers, with half of all patients passing away within three months of their diagnosis. Currently, only about 3% of patients survive for five years once the cancer has spread to other organs. Because of these grim numbers, any new treatment that offers even a small improvement is viewed as a major step forward for patients and their families.
paragraphs.zh: 胰臟癌被廣泛認為是最難治療的疾病之一。《衛報健康》的統計數據顯示，胰臟癌在所有常見癌症中存活率最低，半數患者在確診後的三個月內便會離世。目前，一旦癌症擴散至其他器官，僅有約 3% 的患者能存活超過五年。由於這些數據相當嚴峻，任何能帶來哪怕是些微改善的新療法，都被視為患者及其家屬的一大進展。

paragraphs.en: In a recent early-stage trial involving 61 patients, the results were highly encouraging. According to MedPage Today, 61% of participants saw their tumours shrink or disappear after taking the drug. In about 8% of those cases, the cancer became completely undetectable on medical scans. Furthermore, nearly 77% of the patients were still alive one year after starting the treatment. This is a significant improvement compared to traditional chemotherapy alone, which typically sees only 40% to 45% of patients surviving for one year.
paragraphs.zh: 在近期一項涉及 61 名患者的早期試驗中，結果令人相當振奮。根據《今日醫學頁面》（MedPage Today）報導，61% 的參與者在服用該藥物後，腫瘤出現縮小或消失。在約 8% 的病例中，醫學影像檢查甚至已完全偵測不到癌細胞。此外，近 77% 的患者在開始治療一年後仍然存活。與僅接受傳統化學治療（通常僅有 40% 至 45% 的患者能存活一年）相比，這是一項顯著的進步。

paragraphs.en: Dr. Wungki Park, a cancer specialist at the Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center in New York, presented these findings at a major medical conference in Barcelona. He described the results as being the closest thing to a cure that he has ever seen for patients whose cancer has already spread. Dr. Park noted that the drug does more than just stop growth; it provides a deeper response that helps keep the disease under control for much longer than previous methods. For many patients, this means more time to spend with their loved ones.
paragraphs.zh: 紐約紀念斯隆凱特琳癌症中心（Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center）的癌症專家朴永基（Wungki Park）醫師，在巴塞隆納的一場大型醫學會議上發表了這些研究結果。他形容這些成果是他見過最接近癌症治癒的療法，特別是針對癌症已經擴散的患者。朴醫師指出，該藥物不僅僅是抑制生長，它還能提供更深層的反應，協助患者比以往的方法更長時間地控制病情。對許多患者而言，這意味著能有更多時間與摯愛相處。

paragraphs.en: Despite the excitement, experts are urging the public to remain cautious. Shivan Sivakumar, a researcher at the University of Birmingham, noted that while these results are very promising, they come from a relatively small study that did not include a randomized control group—a standard method used to ensure results are accurate by comparing a treatment group to a group receiving standard care. He emphasized that the findings must be confirmed in larger, more advanced studies, such as the upcoming phase III trial, before the drug can be widely used in hospitals.
paragraphs.zh: 儘管各界感到振奮，專家仍呼籲大眾保持謹慎。伯明罕大學（University of Birmingham）的研究員席凡·席瓦庫瑪（Shivan Sivakumar）指出，雖然這些結果非常有前景，但它們來自規模相對較小的研究，且未包含隨機對照組——這是一種透過比較治療組與接受標準照護組，以確保結果準確性的標準方法。他強調，在該藥物能廣泛應用於醫院之前，這些發現必須在更大規模、更先進的研究（例如即將進行的第三期試驗）中獲得證實。

paragraphs.en: Beyond pancreatic cancer, there is hope that this technology could help treat other types of illness. Because the drug targets a specific gene mutation known as KRAS, which is found in many different cancers, scientists believe it could eventually be used to fight other tumours as well. Michelle Mitchell, the chief executive of Cancer Research UK, stated that while more research is necessary, this development represents a major leap forward. She added that it provides real hope for people facing one of the deadliest forms of cancer.
paragraphs.zh: 除了胰臟癌之外，人們也期盼這項技術能協助治療其他類型的疾病。由於該藥物針對的是一種名為 KRAS 的特定基因突變，而這種突變存在於許多不同的癌症中，科學家認為它最終也可能用於對抗其他腫瘤。英國癌症研究協會（Cancer Research UK）執行長蜜雪兒·米契爾（Michelle Mitchell）表示，雖然仍需更多研究，但這項發展代表了一大躍進。她補充說，這為面對最致命癌症之一的患者提供了真正的希望。

paragraphs.en: As the medical community looks toward the future, the focus will shift to these larger trials. If the results continue to be positive, daraxonrasib could fundamentally change the standard of care for pancreatic cancer. For now, the drug has already received approval from the FDA for specific patients who have already tried other treatments or are unable to receive standard multi-drug therapy. This early approval is a sign of how urgently doctors want to provide new options to those in need.
paragraphs.zh: 隨著醫學界展望未來，焦點將轉向這些更大規模的試驗。如果結果持續正面，daraxonrasib 可能會從根本上改變胰臟癌的標準治療方式。目前，該藥物已獲得美國食品藥物管理局（FDA）核准，適用於已嘗試過其他療法或無法接受標準多重藥物治療的特定患者。這項早期核准顯示了醫師們有多麼迫切地想為有需要的患者提供新選擇。

paragraphs.en: Ultimately, while this pill is not yet considered a final cure, it represents a new era in cancer research. By moving away from relying solely on traditional chemotherapy and toward treatments that target the specific genetic drivers of a disease, doctors are finding new ways to improve the quality and length of life for their patients. The medical world will be watching closely as the next phase of research begins, hoping that this early success will lead to a lasting solution for one of medicine's greatest challenges.
paragraphs.zh: 歸根究底，雖然這種藥丸目前尚未被視為最終的治癒手段，但它代表了癌症研究的新紀元。透過不再僅僅依賴傳統化學治療，轉而採用針對疾病特定基因驅動因素的療法，醫師們正在尋找改善患者生活品質與延長壽命的新途徑。醫學界將密切關注下一階段的研究進展，期盼這項早期的成功，能為醫學界最艱鉅的挑戰之一帶來持久的解決方案。

keyTerms.definitionEn: To praise or acclaim someone or something enthusiastically.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作名詞（冰雹），這裡作動詞，指公開讚揚。文中：A new oral medication called daraxonrasib is being hailed by medical experts as the most significant breakthrough in the treatment of pancreatic cancer in decades.

keyTerms.definitionZh: 令人沮喪的、嚴峻的、不樂觀的。
keyTerms.noteZh: 此處形容數據或情況非常不樂觀，容易被誤認為「殘酷的」。文中：Because of these grim numbers, any new treatment that offers even a small improvement is viewed as a major step forward for patients and their families.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To move or change the focus, direction, or position of something.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作名詞（輪班），這裡作動詞，指焦點的轉移。文中：As the medical community looks toward the future, the focus will shift to these larger trials.

quiz.question: What is the specific one-year survival rate for patients treated with traditional chemotherapy according to the article?
quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據文章第三段，傳統化療的存活率數據明確指出為 40% 到 45%。選項 A 的 3% 是指胰臟癌擴散後的五年存活率；選項 C 的 61% 是指參與試驗中腫瘤縮小的患者比例；選項 D 的 77% 則是使用新藥後一年內的存活比例。這些數據在文中皆有明確區分，讀者需仔細對照。

quiz.question: Why does the medical community require larger, randomized control trials before fully adopting daraxonrasib?

options.A: Because the FDA has already rejected the drug for widespread use.
options.B: Because the drug has been proven to be ineffective for most patients.
options.C: Because the current results may not be scientifically conclusive due to the study's design.
options.D: Because Dr. Wungki Park believes the drug is not yet a complete cure.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。根據文章第五段，研究人員 Shivan Sivakumar 指出目前的試驗規模較小且缺乏隨機對照組（randomized control group），這是確保科學準確性的標準方法，因此必須透過更大型的第三階段試驗來確認結果。選項 A 錯誤，因為 FDA 已給予初步批准；選項 B 與文中提到的正面結果矛盾；選項 D 雖然正確，但並非要求大型試驗的主要科學理由。

quiz.question: In the final paragraph, what does the author mean by the phrase 'genetic drivers of a disease'?

options.A: The biological factors that cause a disease to develop and progress.
options.B: The medical professionals who research genetic mutations.
options.C: The transportation methods used to deliver medicine to cancer cells.
options.D: The side effects caused by chemotherapy treatments.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 A。在文中語境下，'genetic drivers' 指的是導致疾病產生與惡化的基因突變（如第一段提到的 KRAS 突變）。'Driver' 在此處非指駕駛，而是指「驅動因子」。選項 B 將其誤解為人；選項 C 與 D 皆與基因突變的定義無關，屬於對專業術語的錯誤解讀。

quiz.question: What is the primary message of the article regarding daraxonrasib?

options.A: It is a guaranteed cure for all types of cancer.
options.B: It is a promising new treatment that represents a shift toward targeted genetic therapy for pancreatic cancer.
options.C: It is a dangerous drug that should not be used until more tests are done.
options.D: It has completely replaced the need for traditional chemotherapy in all hospital settings.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。全文主旨圍繞在新藥 daraxonrasib 如何透過針對基因突變來治療胰臟癌，雖然目前仍需更多試驗，但這象徵了癌症治療從傳統化療轉向精準醫療的重大進展。選項 A 過度誇大，文中強調尚非「最終治癒」；選項 C 過於負面，忽略了其正面成效；選項 D 錯誤，因為該藥目前是與化療「共同使用」，而非取代。
